\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{صبر} \ur{کرنا} (sabr karnā)}{صبر کرنا (sabr karnā)}]{\ur{صبر} \ur{کرنا} (sabr karnā) — to be patient; to bear a loss calmly}

\label{lesson:UR-C458-sabr-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for integrity, then the Urdu for a promise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{صبر} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{صبر} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{sabr karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be patient; to bear a loss calmly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہمیں} \ur{صبر} \ur{کرنا} \ur{چاہیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hameṅ sabr karnā chāhiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We should be patient.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{صبر} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne sabr kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{صبر} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{sabr karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{صبر}}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ṣabr}, \textquotedblleft{}patience, endurance\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sabr karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sabr karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hameṅ sabr karnā chāhiye.} — We should be patient.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for integrity, then the Urdu for a promise, then say \emph{sabr karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{صبر} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To be patient; to bear a loss calmly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

Before the new one: say the Urdu for a promise, then the Urdu for to be patient.

\end{quote}

\emph{ustād ne baṛe tahammul se savāl sunā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Masculine.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جھڑکنا} (jhiṛaknā)}{جھڑکنا (jhiṛaknā)}]{\ur{جھڑکنا} (jhiṛaknā) — to snap at; to rebuke}

\label{lesson:UR-C458-jhirakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for forbearance, then the Urdu for to put up with.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جھڑکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{جھڑکنا}} — \emph{jhiṛaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to snap at; to rebuke\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ابو} \ur{نے} \ur{بھائی} \ur{کو} \ur{جھڑکا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{abbū ne bhāī ko jhiṛkā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Dad snapped at my brother.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{جھڑکا}, \emph{us ne bachche ko jhiṛkā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جھڑکنا}} (\emph{jhiṛaknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{jhiṛaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to shake, to scold\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{jhaṭ}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5327).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سہنا} (sahnā)}{سہنا (sahnā)}]{\ur{سہنا} (sahnā) — to bear; to suffer patiently}

\label{lesson:UR-C458-sahna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to put up with, then the Urdu for to snap at.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سہنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سہنا}} — \emph{sahnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to bear; to suffer patiently\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دادی} \ur{نے} \ur{بڑا} \ur{دکھ} \ur{سہا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādī ne baṛā dukh sahā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{غم} \ur{سہا}, \emph{us ne gham sahā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سہنا}} (\emph{sahnā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{sáhatē}, \textquotedblleft{}bears, suffers\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13304).
